```{r setup}
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)

# Quieter defaults for every plot in this post, so the examples stay short.
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
)
# update_geom_defaults("point", aes(size = 2, alpha = 0.8))
# update_geom_defaults("smooth", aes(colour = "grey25", linewidth = 0.7))
```

Three types of palettes:

1.  discriminate

2.  qualitative

3.  smooth


### The {ggplot2} default colors

```{r}
#| label: plot-default
ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = class)) +
  geom_smooth()
```

-> not color blindness friendly


### Quick switch to `Okabe-Ito`

```{r}
#| label: plot-okabe-ito
ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = class)) +
  geom_smooth() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = palette.colors(palette = "Okabe-Ito"))
```

The Nature standard in academic publishing. See @wong2011PointsView.

### The same in Python

```{python}
#| label: palette-py
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Okabe-Ito as the default colour cycle (built into matplotlib 3.11+)
okabe_ito = plt.colormaps["okabe_ito"].colors
plt.rcParams["axes.prop_cycle"] = plt.cycler(color=okabe_ito)
```

```{python}
#| label: plot-okabe-ito-python
import pandas as pd

mpg = pd.read_csv(
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/main/data-raw/mpg.csv"
)

for cls, d in mpg.groupby("class"):
    plt.scatter(d.displ, d.hwy, label=cls)
plt.legend()
plt.show()
```
